content:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "observations": [
    {
      "key": "obs_1",
      "facet": "term",
      "statement": "Histogram sort is also known as interpolation sort.",
      "start_line": 12,
      "end_line": 13
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_2",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Histogram sort is a generalization of bucket sort.",
      "start_line": 14,
      "end_line": 16
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_3",
      "facet": "relation",
      "statement": "Histogram sort is a specialization of counting sort.",
      "start_line": 18,
      "end_line": 20
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_4",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Histogram sort is an efficient 3-pass refinement of a bucket sort algorithm.",
      "start_line": 5,
      "end_line": 6
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_5",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "The first pass counts the number of items for each bucket in an auxiliary array and makes a running total so each auxiliary entry is the number of preceding items.",
      "start_line": 7,
      "end_line": 9
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_6",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "The second pass puts each item in its proper bucket according to the auxiliary entry for the key of that item.",
      "start_line": 9,
      "end_line": 10
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_7",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "The last pass sorts each bucket.",
      "start_line": 11,
      "end_line": 11
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_8",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "A bucket sort uses fixed-size buckets.",
      "start_line": 26,
      "end_line": 26
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_9",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "A histogram sort sets up buckets of exactly the right size in a first pass.",
      "start_line": 26,
      "end_line": 26
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_10",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "A counting sort is a histogram sort with one bucket per possible key value.",
      "start_line": 26,
      "end_line": 26
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_11",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "The run time is effectively O(n log log n).",
      "start_line": 30,
      "end_line": 31
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_12",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "R is an approximate rank function to sort the data into n bins.",
      "start_line": 32,
      "end_line": 32
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_13",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "R is an integer valued function into [0, n-1].",
      "start_line": 33,
      "end_line": 33
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_14",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "0 ≤ R(x) ≤ n-1 for x in S.",
      "start_line": 34,
      "end_line": 34
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_15",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "For some x,y in S, R(x)=0 and R(y)=n-1.",
      "start_line": 35,
      "end_line": 35
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_16",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "x < y implies R(x) ≤ R(y) for x,y in S.",
      "start_line": 36,
      "end_line": 36
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_17",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "Each bin then has, on average, 1 entry.",
      "start_line": 37,
      "end_line": 37
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_18",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "Under some rather broad assumptions the number of entries in a bin will be Poisson distributed.",
      "start_line": 37,
      "end_line": 37
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_19",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Allocate an auxiliary integer array H indexed 0 … n-1. Make one pass through the data to count the number of items in each bin, recording the counts in H.",
      "start_line": 38,
      "end_line": 38
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_20",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "The array H is then converted into a cumulative array so each entry in H specifies the beginning bin position of the bin contents in T.",
      "start_line": 38,
      "end_line": 38
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_21",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "Make a second pass through the data. Copy each item x in S from S to T at H(R(x)), then increment H(R(x)) so the next item in the bin goes in the next location in T.",
      "start_line": 38,
      "end_line": 38
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_22",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "The bin number R(x) could be saved in still another auxiliary array to trade off memory for computation.",
      "start_line": 38,
      "end_line": 38
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_23",
      "facet": "mechanism",
      "statement": "For numeric data, a simple R function that works very well is: Let min, max be the minimum and maximum of S. Then R(x) = n*(x - min)/(max-min).",
      "start_line": 39,
      "end_line": 39
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_24",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "This uses quite a bit of extra memory.",
      "start_line": 40,
      "end_line": 40
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_25",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "For large data sets, there could be slow downs because of page faults.",
      "start_line": 40,
      "end_line": 40
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_26",
      "facet": "property",
      "statement": "For large n it is more efficient to bound the number of bins.",
      "start_line": 40,
      "end_line": 40
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_27",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "The note is due to Richard Harter, [email protected], http://www.tiac.net/users/cri/, 8 January 2001, and is used by permission.",
      "start_line": 27,
      "end_line": 29
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_28",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "Author: PEB.",
      "start_line": 41,
      "end_line": 42
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_29",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "Implementation (C and Pascal).",
      "start_line": 43,
      "end_line": 44
    },
    {
      "key": "obs_30",
      "facet": "reference",
      "statement": "See also American flag sort.",
      "start_line": 22,
      "end_line": 23
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "key": "claim_1",
      "status": "DERIVED_INTERPRETATION",
      "statement": "Histogram sort achieves O(n log log n) runtime by using an approximate rank function to distribute items into n bins, resulting in an average of 1 entry per bin with Poisson distribution under broad assumptions.",
      "supported_by": [
        "obs_11",
        "obs_12",
        "obs_17",
        "obs_18"
      ]
    },
    {
      "key": "claim_2",
      "status": "DERIVED_INTERPRETATION",
      "statement": "Histogram sort differs from bucket sort by dynamically sizing buckets in the first pass rather than using fixed-size buckets, and differs from counting sort by potentially having fewer buckets than key values.",
      "supported_by": [
        "obs_8",
        "obs_9",
        "obs_10"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "questions": []
}
